notice: General cosmetic application guidance written for this project. Makeup preferences are subjective; feature-based tips describe common techniques, not rules. No medical claims.

everyday.label: Everyday
everyday.description: Light, quick and comfortable for daily wear.

office.label: Office
office.description: Polished and understated, built to last through the workday.

festive.label: Festive
festive.description: Brighter colour and a little shine for celebrations.

glam.label: Glam
glam.description: Full, defined and long-wearing for evenings and events.

general_cautions: Patch-test new products on a small area first and stop using anything that irritates.
Apply makeup with clean hands and tools, and do not share eye or lip products.

steps.title: Prepare the skin
steps.purpose: Creates a comfortable, even surface so the products that follow apply smoothly.

techniques.default: Apply a small amount to clean skin and let it absorb for about a minute before continuing.
techniques.cream: Warm a pea-sized amount between your fingertips and press it into clean skin; wait about a minute before the next step.
techniques.liquid: Smooth a few drops over clean skin and allow it to absorb before the next step.

steps.title: Prime
steps.purpose: Helps makeup grip and last, and can smooth texture or add glow depending on the formula.

techniques.default: Apply a thin layer where you want makeup to last longest, usually the centre of the face, and let it set briefly.
techniques.gel: Press a thin layer onto areas with visible texture or pores, using patting rather than rubbing motions.
techniques.liquid: Smooth a thin layer over the face with your fingertips and let it set for a minute.

steps.title: Colour-correct (where needed)
steps.purpose: Neutralises localised discolouration such as under-eye darkness or redness before complexion products.

techniques.default: Tap a very small amount only onto the areas you want to neutralise and blend the edges.
techniques.cream: Warm a tiny amount on your fingertip and tap it onto the area; blend the edges softly.
techniques.stick: Dot the stick directly onto the area and tap with a fingertip or small brush to blend.

cautions: Use a thin layer; too much corrector can show through the products on top.

steps.title: Even the complexion
steps.purpose: Evens out skin tone with the level of coverage you prefer.

techniques.default: Start with a small amount at the centre of the face and blend outward, adding more only where needed.
techniques.liquid: Dot a small amount on the forehead, cheeks and chin, then blend outward with a damp sponge or brush.
techniques.stick: Swipe a little onto the centre of the face and blend outward with a dense brush or damp sponge.
techniques.cream: Warm the product on the back of your hand and press it on with a brush or sponge.
techniques.powder: Swirl a brush in the powder, tap off excess and buff onto the skin in circular motions.

steps.title: Conceal
steps.purpose: Adds targeted coverage or brightness where you want it.

techniques.default: Apply a small amount only where needed and tap the edges to blend.
techniques.liquid: Dot a little where needed, wait a few seconds, then tap to blend with a fingertip or sponge.
techniques.cream: Pick up a small amount with a fine brush, press it onto the spot and tap only the edges to blend.

steps.title: Add warmth
steps.purpose: Adds warmth and soft dimension to the face.

techniques.default: Use a light hand and build gradually where light would naturally hit.
techniques.powder: Tap off excess from a fluffy brush and sweep lightly in light layers.
techniques.cream: Tap a small amount on with fingertips or a sponge and blend the edges before it sets.

steps.title: Add colour to the cheeks
steps.purpose: Brings colour and life back to the face after complexion products.

techniques.default: Apply a little to the cheeks and blend the edges so there is no visible line.
techniques.powder: Tap off excess from the brush and sweep lightly, building colour gradually.
techniques.cream: Tap a small amount on with fingertips and blend outward before it sets.
techniques.stick: Dab the stick onto the cheek in two or three dots and blend with fingertips.

steps.title: Highlight
steps.purpose: Reflects light on the high points of the face.

techniques.default: Apply to the high points of the face: tops of the cheekbones, brow bone and bridge of the nose.
techniques.liquid: Tap one small drop onto the tops of the cheekbones and blend the edges with a fingertip.
techniques.powder: Use a small fan or tapered brush and sweep lightly across the tops of the cheekbones.

steps.title: Set
steps.purpose: Sets cream and liquid products to reduce shine and creasing.

techniques.default: Press a light layer onto areas that crease or get shiny, such as under the eyes and the T-zone.
techniques.powder: Tap excess off a puff or brush and press lightly where you need it; avoid dragging over liquid products.

steps.title: Define the brows
steps.purpose: Frames the eyes and fills sparse areas.

techniques.default: Brush the brows up, then fill sparse areas with light strokes following hair direction.
techniques.pencil: Use short, hair-like strokes in sparse areas, then brush through with a spoolie to soften.
techniques.gel: Brush upward and outward through the brows to set them in place.

steps.title: Shape the eyes
steps.purpose: Adds depth and colour to the eyes.

techniques.default: Apply a medium shade across the lid, a deeper shade in the outer corner, and blend all edges.
techniques.powder: Tap off excess, press colour onto the lid and blend the edges with a clean fluffy brush.
techniques.stick: Swipe across the lid close to the lashes and blend upward with a fingertip before it sets.

steps.title: Line the eyes

techniques.default: Draw a line along the upper lash line from the outer corner inward, in short connected strokes.
techniques.liquid: Rest your elbow on a surface and draw short connected strokes along the upper lash line, outer corner first.
techniques.pencil: Draw along the upper lash line and smudge slightly with a small brush for a softer finish.
techniques.gel: Use a fine angled brush to press the liner along the upper lash line in short strokes.

cautions: Avoid the inner waterline if your eyes are sensitive.

steps.title: Define the lashes

techniques.default: Wiggle the wand at the lash roots, then sweep upward to the tips.
techniques.liquid: Wipe excess from the wand, wiggle it at the roots and sweep up to the tips; repeat once if desired.

cautions: Replace mascara regularly and do not share it.

steps.title: Line the lips
steps.purpose: Defines the lip shape and helps lip colour stay in place.

techniques.default: Trace your natural lip line in short strokes, starting at the centre of the upper lip.
techniques.pencil: Trace your natural lip line in short strokes, starting at the centre of the upper lip and working outward.

steps.title: Apply lip colour
steps.purpose: Adds colour to complete the look.

techniques.default: Apply from the centre of the lips outward, following your natural lip line.
techniques.stick: Apply from the centre outward, then press the lips together to even the colour.
techniques.liquid: Apply a thin layer from the centre outward and avoid pressing the lips together until it settles.

steps.title: Finish and set
steps.purpose: Melts powder layers together and can help the look last.

techniques.default: Hold the bottle at arm's length, close your eyes and mist the face in an X and T pattern.
techniques.spray: Hold the bottle at arm's length, close your eyes and mist the face in an X and T pattern; let it dry without touching.

cautions: Keep your eyes closed while spraying.

rules.instruction: Keep the layer thin and concentrate it where you want coverage, letting it fade toward the edges of the face.
rules.rationale: Lighter looks typically use less product.

rules.instruction: For more coverage, build a second thin layer only where needed rather than applying one thick layer.
rules.rationale: Thin layers usually look smoother than one heavy layer.

rules.instruction: Because you prefer full coverage, press (stipple) the product in instead of sweeping it.
rules.rationale: Pressing deposits more product than sweeping.

rules.instruction: Because you prefer light coverage, sheer the product out with a damp sponge.
rules.rationale: A damp sponge lifts excess product.

rules.instruction: Because concealer goes on before foundation in your routine, use a light hand; the foundation will add coverage on top. Blend foundation over it with pressing motions so it is not wiped away.
rules.rationale: Concealer-first workflows rely on foundation to blend edges.

rules.instruction: Apply concealer only where foundation has not already given enough coverage.
rules.rationale: Foundation often reduces how much concealer is needed.

rules.instruction: Tap concealer over the corrected areas without rubbing so the corrector stays in place.
rules.rationale: Rubbing moves the corrector layer.

rules.instruction: Pay attention to the T-zone and under the eyes, where shine and creasing tend to appear first over long wear.
rules.rationale: Long-wear looks benefit from targeted setting.

rules.instruction: Keep to one or two softer shades and blend the edges well for an understated finish.
rules.rationale: Understated looks use fewer, softer shades.

rules.instruction: A single wash of colour across the lid is enough; blend the top edge.
rules.rationale: Quick daily looks.

rules.instruction: Add a shimmer or brighter shade to the centre of the lid for a festive touch.
rules.rationale: Shine reads well at celebrations.

rules.instruction: Deepen the outer corner and crease, and build intensity in layers. In this look eyes are done before foundation so you can clean away any fallout first.
rules.rationale: Doing eyes first lets fallout be removed before the base.

rules.instruction: Keep the line thin and close to the lashes.
rules.rationale: Subtle definition.

rules.instruction: Smudge the line slightly toward the outer corner for a softer, smoky edge.
rules.rationale: Softer definition with more presence.

rules.instruction: Extend the outer end into a small wing, angled toward the end of your brow.
rules.rationale: Defined evening look.

rules.instruction: Apply a second coat once the first has set slightly, combing through any clumps.
rules.rationale: More definition for evening looks.

rules.instruction: Blot once with a tissue for a softer finish that lasts through the day.
rules.rationale: Blotting removes excess product.

rules.instruction: Apply, blot, then apply a second layer for longer wear.
rules.rationale: Layering improves longevity.

rules.instruction: Lightly fill the lips with your liner first so the colour wears more evenly.
rules.rationale: Liner underneath acts as a base.

rules.instruction: You prefer a soft result: start with very little and build gradually.
rules.rationale: Preference.

rules.instruction: You prefer a bolder result: build a second layer once the first is blended.
rules.rationale: Preference.

rules.instruction: A common approach for round faces: apply slightly above the apples of the cheeks and blend up toward the temples.
rules.rationale: Angled placement is commonly used to add length.

rules.instruction: A common approach for oval faces: apply to the apples of the cheeks and blend back along the cheekbone.
rules.rationale: Follows the natural cheek structure.

rules.instruction: A common approach for square faces: apply to the apples in a soft circular motion.
rules.rationale: Rounded placement is commonly used to soften angles.

rules.instruction: A common approach for heart-shaped faces: apply just below the cheekbones and blend outward, keeping colour away from the temples.
rules.rationale: Keeps emphasis away from the wider upper face.

rules.instruction: A common approach for longer faces: apply horizontally across the apples toward the ears.
rules.rationale: Horizontal placement is commonly used to add width.

rules.instruction: A common approach for round faces: sweep bronzer along the temples and just under the cheekbones for definition.
rules.rationale: Adds shadow under the cheekbone.

rules.instruction: A common approach for oval faces: apply where the sun would naturally hit — forehead, cheekbones and the bridge of the nose.
rules.rationale: Natural warmth placement.

rules.instruction: A common approach for square faces: lightly soften the temples and the corners of the jaw.
rules.rationale: Softens angular corners.

rules.instruction: A common approach for heart-shaped faces: apply lightly along the temples and under the cheekbones.
rules.rationale: Balances a wider upper face.

rules.instruction: A common approach for longer faces: apply lightly along the hairline and under the jaw.
rules.rationale: Commonly used to visually shorten the face.

rules.instruction: For almond-shaped eyes most liner styles work; follow the lash line and extend slightly at the outer corner.
rules.rationale: Balanced proportions suit many styles.

rules.instruction: For rounder eyes, thicken the line toward the outer corner and extend it slightly outward to elongate.
rules.rationale: Horizontal emphasis elongates.

rules.instruction: For hooded eyes, keep the line thin and close to the lashes, and draw any wing with your eyes open so it stays visible.
rules.rationale: A lid fold can hide liner drawn with eyes closed.

rules.instruction: For monolids, a slightly thicker line is often needed for it to show with the eyes open; build it gradually.
rules.rationale: Thin lines can disappear when eyes are open.

rules.instruction: For a downturned outer corner, angle the end of the line slightly upward instead of following the lower lash line.
rules.rationale: Commonly used to lift the outer corner.

rules.instruction: For an upturned outer corner, a little liner smudged along the outer lower lash line can balance the shape.
rules.rationale: Balances upward emphasis.

rules.instruction: For hooded eyes, place the crease shade slightly above your natural crease with your eyes open so it remains visible.
rules.rationale: Colour in the natural crease can be hidden.

rules.instruction: For rounder eyes, concentrate deeper shades on the outer third and blend outward.
rules.rationale: Outer emphasis elongates.

rules.instruction: For almond-shaped eyes, most placements work; a deeper shade in the crease adds definition.
rules.rationale: Balanced proportions.

rules.instruction: For monolids, blend colour in a gradient upward from the lash line rather than relying on a crease.
rules.rationale: Gradient placement adds depth without a crease.

rules.instruction: For hooded eyes, focus on lifting at the roots; let the mascara dry before opening your eyes fully to reduce transfer onto the lid.
rules.rationale: Reduces transfer onto the lid fold.
